slot.brief: Give percentage composition of a compound; ask for empirical formula, then molecular formula given molar mass.

stem: A compound contains $63.16\%$ carbon, $12.28\%$ hydrogen and the remainder nitrogen. Its molar mass is $114\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. Find its molecular formula. Use atomic masses C = 12, H = 1 and N = 14.

verdicts.working: For 100 g, mole ratio C:H:N = 63.16/12 : 12.28/1 : 24.56/14 ≈ 3:7:1, giving empirical formula C₃H₇N (mass 57 g mol⁻¹). The molecular mass is 114, so the factor is 2 and the molecular formula is C₆H₁₄N₂.

working:
For $100$ g: $n_{\text{C}}=63.16/12$, $n_{\text{H}}=12.28/1$, $n_{\text{N}}=24.56/14$.
Ratio $=3:7:1$; empirical formula $=\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{N}$, empirical mass $=57$.
Multiplier $=114/57=2$; molecular formula $=\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\text{N}_2$.

Independent check: For 100 g, mole ratio C:H:N = 63.16/12 : 12.28/1 : 24.56/14 ≈ 3:7:1, giving empirical formula C₃H₇N (mass 57 g mol⁻¹). The molecular mass is 114, so the factor is 2 and the molecular formula is C₆H₁₄N₂.
solution:
For $100$ g, the mole ratio is $\frac{63.16}{12}:\frac{12.28}{1}:\frac{24.56}{14}=3:7:1$, so the empirical formula is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{N}$ (empirical mass $=57$).
$$\frac{114}{57}=2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \text{molecular formula}=\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\text{N}_2$$
